thread: Millhaven's dead walked north-northeast toward the ward ring

evidence.clue: A clog standing upright in the lane mud, barefoot prints after it, a gate pushed outward off its post with no latch lifted, mud churned to ridges and holes: many dead left on their own feet. Heavier contamination in the prints than the ground round them.
The girl: feet dragging past the cellar slot, away from the mill toward Pell's, 'hundreds, all night, every night'; they went 'up the north road... Past Pell's. Up the cow way.'

The drove way: parallel grooves, constant-depth toe-down weight a forearm apart, bunching at the old gateposts, nothing downhill; at least sixty heavy marks (Cyndia) four and five abreast 'closer than men would', going north and a little east toward the ring. No mark of any single walker apart. 'They didn't go up our road.' (Jaina)

Sylvanas's dispatch: sixty and more walked out north-northeast toward the outer ring between the Pass and the eastern posts 'a day and more ahead of this'; double the wardens on that stretch and put eyes on the high ground; the Pass road south is clear.
The party did not cross the dead's route on the Ch2 ride (they rode the Pass road two fields and a hedge west).

readerKnows: At least sixty of Millhaven's dead went toward the border on foot, some days ago, by a route the party did not use.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas, Cyndia and the mage know the count floor, the heading and that they are a day or more ahead. They do not know whether the dead are still moving, where they have got to, or what raised them.
notes: The count is a floor, not a final number. 'Rough formation' on page is only 'closer than men would... four and five abreast'; no ranks, no commander. The dispatch is en route (see survivor-girl-and-dispatch). Plan (outside this chapter) places Millhaven's dead burned on the border runestones in Ch9.
